claims.text: Render order: the alarm that means 'somebody built something and never wired it' is first, the good news is last but always present -- a report that only ever nags is a report that gets filtered to a folder nobody opens.
claims.why: KIND_ORDER starts with INVALID_SNAPSHOT and ends with NOW_REACHED; NOW_REACHED is the only good news and is last.

claims.text: NOW_REACHED is good news. TEST_ONLY is a real finding that deliberately does not block: a test is evidence of intent, and failing a build over it would get the gate switched off. It is loud instead -- its own kind, its own list in the snapshot, its own count in the diff.
claims.why: The claim about being loud with its own list and count in the snapshot is not observable in this chunk; only the set membership is defined here.

claims.text: What an acceptance may cover. Acceptance hygiene, a broken snapshot and a changed ignore configuration are deliberately NOT acceptable: 'the acceptance list is wrong', 'the snapshot contradicts itself' and 'this run looked at less of the tree than the baseline did' have to be repaired, not waived.
claims.why: ACCEPTABLE_KINDS excludes INVALID_SNAPSHOT, IGNORE_DRIFT, STALE_ACCEPTANCE, INVALID_ACCEPTANCE, TEST_ONLY, and NOW_REACHED; the named categories are not in the set.

claims.text: Built once per run, then queried per switch name. Fenced blocks and generated files are dropped at BUILD time rather than at query time, so there is exactly one place where 'does this text count' is decided.
claims.why: build() filters generated files and fenced blocks; sites() only searches the pre-built lines.

claims.text: Non-alphanumerics collapse to single spaces before counting, so ``PKG_TURBO=1`` scores 1, not 12: punctuation and the value are not an explanation of what the switch turns on.
claims.why: _described replaces the name with a space and collapses non-alphanumerics via _ALNUM_RUN.sub(' ', rest).strip() before length comparison.

claims.text: What was excluded from this run, as a comparable fingerprint. Recorded in the snapshot so that a run narrowed by ``DAEDALUS_IGNORE`` can never be mistaken for a clean one. The env value is stored VERBATIM rather than hashed: the point is that a reviewer reading the failure can see what was hidden without re-running anything.
claims.why: The function returns {'env': os.environ.get(IGNORE_ENV, '').strip(), 'file': hashed first 16 chars}; the env value is stored verbatim and the file content is hashed.

claims.text: The mechanical state. ``state`` is what the snapshot stores; ``sites`` is runtime-only detail (file:line) used to make remedies actionable, and is deliberately kept OUT of the snapshot so line-number churn never produces a diff a human has to read. ``reach`` and ``switches`` are the reports this state was derived FROM, carried out so no caller has to re-run either engine to ask a follow-up question.
claims.why: The docstring claims sites are kept out of the snapshot and reach/switches are carried for follow-up, but this chunk only defines the dataclass fields; the snapshot serialization is elsewhere.

claims.text: A git object name, and the shortest abbreviation that is an identifier rather than a coincidence. git's own floor is 7; a 1-character 'prefix' matches roughly one HEAD in sixteen, and a check that passes by accident is worse than no check because it is believed.
claims.why: _MIN_ABBREV is 7 and _SHA_RE enforces at least 7 hex characters.

claims.text: WHICH TREE this scan looked at: ``head``, ``branch``, ``dirty``. The digest proves nobody hand-edited the snapshot. It says NOTHING about when the snapshot was taken -- a baseline generated thirty commits ago verifies its own digest perfectly, and that gap was measured doing real damage: the self-improvement loop suppressed the stale hand-written inventory (which has a freshness gate) while trusting a stale generated snapshot (which had none), and acted on a description of a tree that no longer existed.
claims.why: The digest claim and the historical damage description are not verifiable in this chunk; the function returns head, branch, dirty only.

claims.text: ``head`` is the authority and is covered by the digest (see :func:`_digest`). There is deliberately NO ``generated_at``: a clock reading answers 'when did the generator run', which is the weaker question, and it would destroy the byte-identity this artifact is built on -- see :func:`snapshot_bytes`.
claims.why: The digest coverage and the absence of generated_at are not observable in this chunk; _digest and snapshot_bytes are defined elsewhere in the file.

claims.text: ``dirty`` is probed only when there is a ``.git`` to probe, so a scan of a tree that is not a checkout costs no subprocess and still answers honestly: ``None`` means 'could not tell', never 'clean'.
claims.why: The function probes dirty only if probe_dirty is True and head != 'unknown'; render_mod._dirty is called which likely checks for .git, and the verdict maps to True, False, or None.

claims.text: FAILS CLOSED on the artifact's own defects -- an absent, non-string or malformed ``repo_state.head`` means the snapshot cannot say what it scanned, and a snapshot that cannot say what it scanned is not evidence about this tree. That is the opposite of the map's digest rule, and deliberately so: the digest asks 'did a human edit this', where a missing field is a plausible degradation; this asks 'does this describe me', where a missing field is the whole failure.
claims.why: The function returns fresh: False with a reason when repo_state.head is missing, non-string, or empty after strip; it does not fall back to True.

claims.text: FAILS OPEN when the recorded head is well-formed and git cannot answer at all: a tarball checkout with no ``.git`` is not evidence of staleness, and turning 'I cannot tell' into 'refuse everything' is a worse failure than ranking. Same rule, same reasoning, as ``daedalus.spine.picker.inventory_freshness``.
claims.why: The fails-open branch is beyond the end of this chunk (the code cuts off at the _SHA_RE.fullmatch check); the actual handling of git unavailability is not visible here.

observations.what: The chunk ends mid-function in snapshot_freshness; the fails-open behavior described in the docstring cannot be verified from this window.
repo_state imports render_mod from within the function, which is unusual but works; it may create a circular import risk if render imports drift at module level.
DocIndex.build reads files with errors='replace', so unreadable bytes become replacement characters; this could mask encoding issues but is a deliberate choice.

The comment about 'a check that passes by accident is worse than no check' is a policy statement; the code enforces a minimum abbreviation of 7 but does not itself prevent accidental matches beyond the regex.

ACCEPTABLE_KINDS excludes TEST_ONLY and NOW_REACHED, but the comment says acceptance hygiene, broken snapshot, and changed ignore config are not acceptable; the set also excludes INVALID_ACCEPTANCE, STALE_ACCEPTANCE, INVALID_SNAPSHOT, and IGNORE_DRIFT, which aligns with the comment.
